requiredScope: The complete required language and role scope remains in force.

Mutation/InsertQuery.role: An ordered write of the native cells produced by an independent checked SELECT.
Mutation/InsertQuery.structure: One destination, one checked SELECT with explicitly typed output roles and one detached RETURNING layout.
Mutation/InsertQuery.conditions: Output width and native kind agree with the exact write slot at each position. The definition is unbounded and unordered. Signed expressions remain within the int4 role. Text uses a resolved native text reference or literal. Explicit NULL inhabits the owning destination's kind. The complete root verifies the return coordinates over the target.
Mutation/InsertQuery.meaning: Interpret the independent SELECT once for its scoped input rows, filter and duplicate policy. Insert every projected row in that fixed value correspondence and use native defaults for omitted slots.
Mutation/InsertQuery.sql: Write the exact target layout and the producing SELECT. Type a NULL with the corresponding native destination kind and preserve source aliasing and DISTINCT.

externalInterpretation: Use the same resolved ordinary input relations and the same writable destination. The input fixture has repeated, distinct and nullable native rows; the target fixture has known values and defaults.
observations: Preserve text values, exact target position, native result metadata and affected rows.
Preserve input duplicate policy, source predicates and zero-row writes.
Preserve SQL NULL distinctly from empty text and omit fields with native defaults.
Observe the exact target before and after the statement and restore both input and output fixture relations.

finite.completeness: Recover origin, positional native layout, NULL form or filter, and duplicate policy from each observed constructed value.

exploration.requiredForms: Vary text field roles, typed constants, explicit NULL, no rows, native int4 positions, DISTINCT and returned slots.

analysis: Insert a bare text projection into a resolved text slot.

Read a text field from an explicitly aliased independent source under a text presence predicate.
negative: Directly give a signed expression to a native text target.

faults: Read the other source text field for the same destination.
